questions.question: What does Now in Android do, and who runs or learns from it?
questions.answer: It is a Kotlin/Jetpack Compose Android news app and reference implementation for developers. Users browse Android-development videos/articles, follow topics and receive matching-content notifications. Developers can run the demo flavor using local data; the README says the prod backend is not publicly available.
requiredFacts: Demo local data differs from unavailable public prod backend

evidence.excerpt:
This is the repository for the [Now in Android](https://developer.android.com/series/now-in-android)
app. It is a **work in progress** 🚧.

**Now in Android** is a fully functional Android app built entirely with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. It
follows Android design and development best practices and is intended to be a useful reference
for developers. As a running app, it's intended to help developers keep up-to-date with the world
of Android development by providing regular news updates.

The app is currently in development. The `prodRelease` variant is [available on the Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.samples.apps.nowinandroid).

# Features

**Now in Android** displays content from the
[Now in Android](https://developer.android.com/series/now-in-android) series. Users can browse for
links to recent videos, articles and other content. Users can also follow topics they are interested
in, and be notified when new content is published which matches interests they are following.

The app also uses
[product flavors](https://developer.android.com/studio/build/build-variants#product-flavors) to
control where content for the app should be loaded from.

The `demo` flavor uses static local data to allow immediate building and exploring of the UI.

The `prod` flavor makes real network calls to a backend server, providing up-to-date content. At 
this time, there is not a public backend available.

For normal development use the `demoDebug` variant. For UI performance testing use the
`demoRelease` variant.

questions.question: Name the principal Now in Android components and responsibilities.
questions.answer: app contains activity, app composition and navigation scaffolding; feature api modules publish navigation keys and impl modules hold feature UI/ViewModels; core:data coordinates data sources; core:datastore persists preferences; core:database stores Room data; core:network handles remote requests. Equivalent Gradle path notation is accepted; features are split api/impl modules, not a single implied module.
requiredFacts: feature api keys and impl UI/ViewModels are separate
core:datastore persists data and core:database uses Room

evidence.excerpt:
### The `app` module
This contains app level and scaffolding classes that bind the rest of the codebase, such as
`MainActivity`, `NiaApp` and app-level controlled navigation. A good example of this is the navigation setup through `NiaNavHost` and the bottom navigation bar setup through `TopLevelDestination`. The `app` module depends on all `feature` modules and required `core` modules.

### Feature modules 
These are feature-specific modules that handle a single responsibility in the app. For example, the `ForYou` feature handles all content and UI state for the "ForYou" screen. Feature modules aren't Gradle modules themselves, they are split into two submodules: 

* `api` - contains navigation keys
* `impl` - contains everything else

This approach allows features to navigate to other features by using the target feature's navigation keys. A feature's `api` and `impl` modules can be used by any app, including test or other flavoured apps. If a class is needed only by one feature module, it should remain within that module. If not, it should be placed into an appropriate `core` module. 

A feature's `api` module should not depend on another feature's `api` or `impl` module. A feature's `impl` should only depend on another feature's `api` module. Both submodules should only depend on the `core` modules that they require. 

### Core modules 
These are common library modules containing auxiliary code and specific dependencies that
  need to be shared between other modules in the app. These modules can depend on other core
  modules, but they shouldn’t depend on feature nor app modules.

feature:1:impl,
feature:2:impl
... Functionality associated with a specific feature or user journey. Typically contains UI components and ViewModels which read data from other modules.
Examples include:
  • feature:topic:impl displays information about a topic on the TopicScreen.
  • feature:foryou:impl which displays the user's news feed, and onboarding during first run, on the For You screen.

questions.question: Which languages, frameworks, build system and module boundaries organize Now in Android?
questions.answer: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose implement the Android app; Gradle Kotlin DSL declares app/core/feature/sync modules, including bookmark api and impl. settings.gradle.kts includes the build-logic composite build and requires JDK17+. Hilt is used for dependency injection. Source packages alone are not Gradle module boundaries.
requiredFacts: Gradle Kotlin DSL with explicitly included modules

evidence.excerpt:
**Now in Android** is a fully functional Android app built entirely with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. It
follows Android design and development best practices and is intended to be a useful reference
for developers. As a running app, it's intended to help developers keep up-to-date with the world
of Android development by providing regular news updates.

# Development Environment

**Now in Android** uses the Gradle build system and can be imported directly into Android Studio (make sure you are using the latest stable version available [here](https://developer.android.com/studio)). 

Change the run configuration to `app`.

To facilitate testing of components, **Now in Android** uses dependency injection with
[Hilt](https://developer.android.com/training/dependency-injection/hilt-android).

Most data layer components are defined as interfaces.
Then, concrete implementations (with various dependencies) are bound to provide those interfaces to
other components in the app.

questions.question: Where does the selected Android launcher execution begin?
questions.answer: app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml declares .NiaApplication and .MainActivity with MAIN/LAUNCHER intent filter. Android invokes MainActivity.onCreate, which calls setContent and composes NiaApp within providers/theme. The framework lifecycle invocation is a declared entry boundary, not a statically called Kotlin main.
requiredFacts: NiaApp is composed; Android lifecycle is external dispatch

questions.question: Where is X = removing a saved news resource while offering undo implemented?
questions.answer: BookmarksViewModel.removeFromSavedResources in feature/bookmarks/impl launches in viewModelScope, enables shouldDisplayUndoBookmark, remembers lastRemovedBookmarkId and calls UserDataRepository.setNewsResourceBookmarked(id,false). undoBookmarkRemoval launches a true write for the remembered ID then clears undo state. Coroutine scheduling is not proven by static calls alone.
requiredFacts: viewModelScope coroutine sets undo flag and remembered id
undoBookmarkRemoval requests true and clears undo state

questions.question: Which internal modules does A = core:data directly declare as production dependencies?
questions.answer: core/data/build.gradle.kts declares api edges to core:common, core:database, core:datastore and core:network, plus implementation edges to core:analytics and core:notifications. core:datastore-test and core:testing are testImplementation only. The direction is core:data -> these modules; it is not a claim that every repository executes them.
requiredFacts: Manifest directions do not imply every method executes dependencies

questions.question: For R = removeFromSavedResources(id), trace the source-supported production path to preference removal and identify dispatch boundaries.
questions.answer: BookmarksScreen wires removeFromBookmarks to the ViewModel method. That method launches a coroutine and calls the UserDataRepository interface with false. DataModule binds that interface to OfflineFirstUserDataRepository, whose override delegates to NiaPreferencesDataSource and then logs analytics. The data source calls DataStore.updateData, copies preferences, and removes the ID from bookmarkedNewsResourceIds for false; IOException is caught/logged. Hilt provisioning, coroutine scheduling and DataStore execution are external framework boundaries; this static path is not a runtime trace or disk-write success proof.
requiredFacts: Screen callback points to ViewModel method
ViewModel calls UserDataRepository with false in coroutine
Repository delegates to preferences and logs analytics
Preferences update removes map key and catches IOException

@Composable
internal fun BookmarksScreen(
    onTopicClick: (String) -> Unit,
    onShowSnackbar: suspend (String, String?) -> Boolean,

questions.question: If Y = BookmarksViewModel.removeFromSavedResources changes, which direct screen/test consumers are evidenced?
questions.answer: BookmarksScreen passes the method reference as removeFromBookmarks; BookmarksViewModelTest calls it in removal and undo scenarios. The method-reference dependency is direct, but actual user-click dispatch requires Compose callback execution. Changes may alter feed/undo observations; this does not prove unrelated feature screens depend on this ViewModel method.
requiredFacts: Behavioral effects and user invocation are conditional, not inferred whole-app reachability

questions.question: Which tests exercise X, and how do they enter its implementation?
questions.answer: BookmarksViewModelTest.oneBookmark_whenRemoving_removesFromFeed seeds a bookmark, subscribes to feedUiState, calls viewModel.removeFromSavedResources and asserts empty Success feed plus undo visibility. feedUiState_undoneBookmarkRemoval_bookmarkIsRestored calls removal then undo and checks one item plus hidden undo. These are source-inspected tests, not a claimed executed device or persistence test.

Undo test invokes undo and asserts restoration

questions.question: Where does Z = newsResourceId plus bookmarked boolean enter and become persistent preference data?
questions.answer: NiaPreferencesDataSource.setNewsResourceBookmarked accepts ID/boolean. DataStore.updateData copies UserPreferences and puts id->true for true or removes the key for false, with IOException logged. The userData flow maps bookmarkedNewsResourceIdsMap.keys into UserData.bookmarkedNewsResources. This is an ID set represented by map keys, not a stored false-valued bookmark entry.
requiredFacts: Data source accepts id and boolean
true puts id->true; false removes key
updateData wraps preference copy and catches IOException
Read flow uses map keys as bookmarked resource IDs
